clearedSpotChecks.check: Whether MegaETH's revm fork changes a result of the PoolManager bytecode: the 37 source files of megaeth-labs/revm main crates/interpreter compared with the crates.io revm-interpreter 37.0.3 sources, and the PoolManager runtime scanned for the bytes of the opcodes the fork can enable early.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I downloaded revm-interpreter 37.0.3 from static.crates.io and fetched arithmetic.rs, bitwise.rs, control.rs, i256.rs, system.rs, memory.rs and utility.rs from raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/revm/main/crates/interpreter/src/instructions/. All seven are byte-equal to the stock crate. The fork's shared_memory.rs resize wrapper returns true unconditionally. I fetched the runtime with eth_getCode on mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc (0xacb7...d38e) and on rpc.monad.xyz (0x188d...a8e): both are 24,009 bytes, an opcode walk that skips push data finds no 0xe6, 0xe7, 0xe8, 0xa7 or 0xae, and the only 0xfe is at offset 23,996. The item holds.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-1297: per-PoolManager counts of the operand classes that the evmone-compiler master handlers compute wrongly, from the cycle 33 census of validated MegaETH blocks, extended by a census run of the public stateless validator over all 23 blocks with a PoolManager log from 32,983,020 to 32,994,402.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched lib/compiler/aot_instructions.hpp from both the aot-compiler and master branches of megaeth-labs/evmone-compiler. Both have sha256 5812d1bcf6de21ac..., and the handlers are faulty as described. sar ORs in sign_mask << (256 - y), byte shifts by 31 - n bits instead of bytes, and signextend builds its mask with 1u << (b - 1), which is undefined behaviour once b reaches 32. The census file results.jsonl holds 23 entries, all with status validated. For block 32,994,234 I checked on chain that eth_getBlockByNumber returns hash 0x2089da4d...1f7e, the same hash the census recorded, and that eth_getLogs returns one PoolManager Swap log (topic 0x40e9cecb). I did not rerun the validator. The argument holds for past blocks: a producer state that differs from the stock interpreter fails the comparison. It does not cover a future producer build, and the item already says so.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Upcoming Monad forks: every proposal on the MIP index that earlier cycles did not record (MIP-14, 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24), assuming each ships.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched MIP-19, MIP-23 and MIP-24 from mips.monad.xyz. All three are Draft. MIP-19 states that contracts are exempt from the current reserve balance checks and defines SETCODEFROM as 0xA7, which the PoolManager runtime does not contain in executable code (scan above). MIP-23 says recording a configuration for an ordinary contract does not make that contract subject to the EOA reserve restriction. MIP-24 says the precompile at 0x1002 MUST return exactly 32 bytes, zero on failure, and MUST NOT revert. A short input is a failure, so a 68-byte transfer call returns the zero word. Currency.transfer then sets success to false, because it requires mload(0) == 1 or empty return data (src/types/Currency.sol:59-72), and take reverts. A balanceOf read returns 0. Only the caller's own currency id 0x1002 is affected and no other user holds it. I did not refetch MIP-14, 16, 17, 20, 21 or 22.
